title: C generic Rule255 fallback decodes without payload validation; Rust/Python validate full IPv6 structure (cross-impl divergence)
description: Found by robustness review pass of project-LICHEN-worker6-1dft (P2, pre-existing - NOT introduced by the ingress-ceiling change; the new test pins the lenient behavior so it looks like a parity test). C generic dispatcher rule255/uncompressed fallback (lichen/subsys/schc/schc.c, post-ceiling) is a bare memcpy of the payload: it accepts EMPTY payloads and non-IPv6 bytes and returns success. Rust decode_rule255 (rust/lichen-schc/src/codec.rs:1459-1468) runs validate_full_ipv6_structure on the payload (version 6, exact lengths, ext-header walk, UDP checksums); Python decode_rule255 (python/src/lichen/schc/headers.py:201-213) runs validate_full_ipv6. So data_len==1 rule255 -> C returns 0 (success with zero-length delivery; lichen_link_rx.c:353 only tests ret<0 so it would report success with out_len 0), Rust/Python return errors. Per spec/03-adaptation.md Rule255: 'Its payload MUST be a complete, structurally valid IPv6 packet'. Fix: mirror Rust/Python - route the generic fallback payload through the same structural validation (the C per-rule decompressors' validate_ipv6_transport_lengths/validate_ipv6_header_chain machinery exists in schc_helpers.c; reuse it for the rule255 payload), keeping the RX/TX address-policy split (emission policy NOT applied on receipt). Decide the zero-payload/short-payload edge (< IPV6_HDR_LEN -> reject as malformed). Then re-pin tests/schc test_rule255_ingress_profile_ceiling with a NON-IPv6 payload to assert rejection parity with Rust/Python (current 0x41-fill vector would flip from accepted to rejected). Coordinate with hahk/7v5f (non-IPv6 Rule255 emission on the compress side) - same spec sentence governs both directions.
